title: Buglands
summary: A concept to retheme the Costa Rica Climber as Buglands, a playground of bug habitats.
overview: Concept work to retheme the Costa Rica Climber in Thanksgiving Point’s Butterfly Biosphere. The play structure was not really working, and there was not much theming. Jayden walked the climber and photographed it, then developed Buglands: regions themed to different kinds of bugs. He built a concept deck for the whole idea and modeled a few touchpoints.
role: Concept designer. Site research, the theme and story, the concept deck, and initial 3D touchpoint models.
challenge: Retheme the existing Costa Rica Climber. It was not really working as a play structure, and the space had little theming.
heroCaption: Opening slide of the concept deck, “The Buglands.”
heroAlt: Concept illustration from the Buglands deck, titled The Buglands.

regions.name: Colony Cliffs
regions.text: Bug communities: ants, termites, and social wasps. In the deck this is the entrance, where colony builders make tunnels, chambers, and towers.

regions.name: Hopper Plains
regions.text: The toddler area. Grassland and grasshoppers: soft fields for bouncing, leaping, and playing from a grasshopper’s view.

regions.name: Wetland Wonders
regions.text: Water habitat: diving beetles, water striders, whirligigs, and scorpions in arid riverbeds. The deck also calls this Bug Basin.

regions.name: Bug Borough
regions.text: Underground or forest-floor bugs. Tunnels, bioluminescence, glowworms, isopods, beetles, roaches, and decomposers.

regions.name: Canopy Crossing
regions.text: Above, in the rainforest canopy: tropical insects, stick bugs, and assassin bugs. The deck splits the canopy into Build a Bug, Find a Bug, Fly a Bug, and the Butterfly Passage.

title: Jurassic Jungle: Shoe Room Story Video
summary: A video for the shoe-room monitor, so guests understand the story before they enter the playground.
overview: Jurassic Jungle is a kids’ playground with a story throughout. Kids wear interactive wristbands to log their progress as they find missing hatchlings and return them to their nest. Jayden owned the touchpoint in the shoe room, before guests enter.
role: Designer and motion/video creator for the touchpoint (After Effects).
challenge: Help guests understand the story and the instructions before they enter the chaotic playground. Signage was already there. Early on, very few people stopped to read it, and guests were saying they didn’t know what was going on at first. The task was a video for the monitor, to increase dwell time and understanding.
steps: Observations, logging insights in a document.
Planned the key messages to deliver.
Built it in After Effects over several iterations, optimizing the visuals to minimize confusion and using animation to direct attention.
Installed the video on the TV.
Fixed the issues that showed up — volume, and the time between loops — and shipped edits for day 2.
outcome: After the video was installed, he observed more dwell time and more attention from both kids and parents. That read is qualitative. No counts were recorded.
